unsupported_claims: Breadth-first exploration captures structural equivalence and depth-first exploration captures homophily; the evidence does not state this BFS/DFS mapping.

Node2vec uses a biased second-order random walk with return parameter p and in-out parameter q to interpolate between BFS-like and DFS-like sampling; the evidence mentions a 2nd order random walk but not p, q, or the BFS/DFS interpolation.
rationale: The hierarchical softmax claims (expensive normalization over all vertices, binary tree, O(log|V|) vs O(|V|)) and node2vec's motivation (rigid neighborhoods, need to capture both communities and roles) are supported. The BFS/DFS mapping and the p/q parameters go beyond the provided evidence, though they are accurate background about node2vec.
